clue.text: Making an issue of what's been written?

definitions.text: Making an issue of what's been written?

parts.words: Making an issue of what's been written?
parts.note: an issue of a magazine or book is an edition put out to the public, so making one from written work is the trade of bringing it out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making an issue' sounds like stirring up a fuss over a text; it is the business of putting writing out in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing an issue of a book or paper into being is exactly the work of a printing and distribution house.

clue.text: Vegetable bringing in ready money once

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A vegetable seller takes in cash on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money once' means a currency no longer used: Spain's, before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Spain's unit of currency until the euro replaced it, hence former money.

clue.text: Obscure outbreak starts with Belgium not France

indicators.note: starts with points to the first letter of the word for outbreak as the one to change
not marks which letter goes out in favour of the other

parts.note: a flurry is a sudden outbreak of activity
F is the international code for France
B is the international code for Belgium

explanation.surface: An obscure epidemic begins in Belgium rather than France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indistinct or unclear in outline can be described as fuzzy, so it is a synonym for obscure.

clue.text: Discharge from lemon — impatient to get cleaned up

indicators.note: cleaning up a mess sorts it into new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Juice squirts from a lemon, and someone impatient wants it wiped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a leak; it is carrying out duties.
explanation.definitionFit: The discharge of duties is their carrying out, the execution or fulfilment of a plan.

clue.text: Populace's vote given to Hearts with two narrow away wins

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: the vote is handed in among the other letters, placed between them
two says the score for a narrow away win is used twice

parts.note: a narrow away win in football is a 0-1 score, read as the letters O and I
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A football crowd votes for Hearts, the Edinburgh club, after two tight wins on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is an Edinburgh football club, but here it is the card suit; the narrow away win is a 0-1 scoreline read as letters. The 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek phrase meaning 'the many' is used for the common people, the general masses.

clue.text: On the up, some prosper eventually — or not

indicators.note: On the up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rising few may succeed in the end, or perhaps they won't.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'On the up' reads upwards, so the hidden letters run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not at any time' is an emphatic denial, the strongest way to say no rather than yes.

clue.text: Italian church passion

explanation.surface: A fervent Italian churchgoer's devotion, or the passions stirred in a church in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or strong desire, so it serves as a synonym for a passion for something.

clue.text: Rest found here in Bill and Ben's garden?

definitions.text: Rest found here in Bill and Ben's garden?

parts.words: Rest found here in Bill and Ben's garden?
parts.note: Bill and Ben, the Flowerpot Men of a British children's TV show, looked identical; a garden's flower plots would be theirs, and paired sleeping places are where one rests

explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the identical Flowerpot Men of 1950s British children's television; flower plots in their garden become a matched pair of sleeping places.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of matching single sleeping places in one room is where two people rest separately.

clue.text: Bad manners where driving is fastest?

parts.note: high describes meat or game that has gone off, smelling bad
ways means habits or manners

explanation.surface: Rude behaviour on the roads where people drive quickest.
explanation.definitionFit: Main public roads are the routes where speed limits are highest, so traffic moves quickest there.

clue.text: Something printed from two journalists I crashed into south of border

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of means placed below, so the later letters come after the border word

parts.note: a limit is a border or boundary

indicators.note: two says the word for a journalist is used twice

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: crashed suggests wrecked and broken, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two reporters and the narrator crash their car beyond the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A restricted print run, such as a numbered book or art print, is one item printed in a fixed quantity.

clue.text: Shabby inner-city parking causes depression

parts.note: a slum is a run-down, shabby district in a city's inner area
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Run-down urban parking is blamed for making people feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood; it is the economic sense, a sharp downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slide or downturn is called a depression, and the same word names a sudden fall in trade or prices.

clue.text: Charging in, verbalising

parts.note: to verbalise a thought is to put it into words, to give voice to it

explanation.surface: Someone bursting into a room while talking, an attacker charging in shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging in' reads as rushing forward; 'Charging' alone is the definition, billing a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a customer means billing them, which is what sending out a bill or account for payment does.

clue.text: Trooped off to see something exploding

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the clue word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched away to watch a blast go off.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval missile that travels underwater and detonates on hitting a ship is a thing that explodes.

clue.text: Colourful bit of scenery drops — sign the show's over

parts.note: rain is drops of water falling from the sky
performers take a bow at the end of a show

explanation.surface: A painted backdrop falls on stage, a signal that the play has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful bit of scenery' suggests a stage flat; it is an arc of colours in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of seven colours seen in the sky after a shower is a vivid part of the natural landscape.

clue.text: Communist allowed ground-up dry tea for celebration

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
to let is to allow

indicators.note: ground up means crushed into small bits, so the letters of the words that follow are broken and remixed

explanation.surface: A communist permits tea leaves to be crushed for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorable, happy occasion is called this, from the way saints' days and festivals were printed in red on calendars.

clue.text: Island folk project a hit, Ian Stewart boasts

indicators.note: boasts in the sense of has or contains, so the answer lies inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Stewart says the islanders' venture will be a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boasts' sounds like bragging but means contains.
explanation.definitionFit: People native to the largest island of French Polynesia, in the South Pacific, are islanders.

clue.text: Spirits seen in German city church steeple's entrance

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: entrance points to the first letter, the way in to the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: Ghosts glimpsed at the door of a church steeple in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated extracts distilled from plants are called spirits, a synonym for these extracts.

clue.text: Brief time in front of grave around memorial showing grief

indicators.note: around means these letters go round the memorial, holding it inside

parts.note: MO is short for moment

indicators.note: front of points to the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: an urn holding ashes acts as a memorial

explanation.surface: A short pause at the graveside around a memorial expresses sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' sends the first group of pieces round the memorial, so the urn ends up in the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of bereavement or lamenting a loss is how a grieving person behaves.

clue.text: Electrical fault noticed with restricted observation?

parts.note: a short is a short circuit, a common electrical fault
sighted means seen or noticed

explanation.surface: A wiring problem was spotted during a limited inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to see distant things clearly has limited vision, a form of myopia; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Strange dusk gathers over uniform figures in square

indicators.note: gathers means takes in, so the jumbled word holds a letter inside
strange means odd or out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: O is short for over in cricket scoring
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An eerie twilight closes in over a uniformed squad drilling in a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' makes SUDK from DUSK; 'gathers' puts O inside after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese-named puzzle has digits arranged in a nine-by-nine grid, so numbers placed in a grid.

clue.text: Playing lines United used to replace energy once

indicators.note: used to replace says one letter goes in where another came out
once says only one of the two energy letters is swapped

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry
E is the symbol for energy in physics
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: An actor's lines are shared with a team, swapping in vigour once.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSES has two Es; only the second becomes U.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, one side meeting another is described as 'against' it, as in Spurs playing Arsenal.

clue.text: Slip put right near the back of a book

definitions.text: Slip put right near the back of a book

parts.words: Slip put right near the back of a book
parts.note: a slip is a mistake, and also a slip of paper; a list of corrected printing mistakes is often placed at the end of a book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' does double duty: a mistake, and the small sheet listing corrections that publishers insert.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a noted correction of a printing mistake, often listed on a page or slip at the end of a volume.

clue.text: Coming from the south, one's goal to make US city

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming from the south means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: one's means one is, I'm, I being one
an aim is a goal

explanation.surface: A traveller from the southern states aims to reach a big American city.
explanation.definitionFit: This Florida city on the Atlantic coast is a major American metropolis.

clue.text: Praise British university breaking routine

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the word for routine so the other letters can go inside

parts.note: trite means routine, hackneyed

explanation.surface: Commendation for a British university that breaks with the usual way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech or gift honouring someone is an expression of admiration, and so a form of commendation.

clue.text: Food giving a chap toil when cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being mixed and transformed, so the letters of the words before are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man labours in the kitchen to produce something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin pork sausage is an item of food, here given by the broad category.

clue.text: Makes more flat golfing equipment

definitions.meaning: smooths out creases in clothes with a hot appliance
golf clubs with angled metal heads, numbered three to nine

explanation.surface: A golfer flattening the lie or ironing the club cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing laundry flattens it; and the metal-headed clubs in a golf bag share the name.

clue.text: Revolutionary 'Something in the Air', with a narrative

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning over, so the word for something in the air is read backwards

parts.note: gas is something present in the air; the quoted title is also a 1969 hit song

explanation.surface: A rebel band's song title paired with a story, like a record review.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted song title 'Something in the Air' (by Thunderclap Newman) is just a description of a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, involved story, originally an Icelandic tale of heroes, is a kind of narrative.

clue.text: Disregarding odds, unties astern — the US task, finding wartime havens

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters means only the even letters of the following words are kept

explanation.surface: A boat casts off from the stern while Americans complete their mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disregarding odds' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters across 'unties astern the US task', giving NISSEN then HUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: These corrugated-iron semicircular buildings gave soldiers shelter in both World Wars, so they were wartime refuges.
